question: Which year's budget was called a Black Budget of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1973-74**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The budget referred to as the **"Black Budget"** of India was the **1973-74 Union Budget**.
 
• **Fiscal Deficit**: Known as the "Black Budget" due to a high fiscal deficit of ₹550 crore.
 
• **Presented by**: Yashwantrao B Chavan, the Finance Minister at the time.
 
• **Date**: February 28, 1973.
 
• **Context**: Introduced during severe financial difficulties and economic turmoil in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Union Budget is an annual financial statement that the Government of India presents to outline its estimated revenue and expenditure for the coming fiscal year.
 
• Traditionally presented by the Finance Minister of India in February. The budget session is usually held in Parliament.
 
• **Landmark Budgets**: 
 
 
• **Black Budget (1973-74)**: Known for its high fiscal deficit.
 
• **Epochal Budget (1991)**: Marked the beginning of economic liberalization.
 
• **Carrot and Stick Budget (1986)**: Introduced the MODVAT system.
